title: world.counters gpu reports the world's sdf.world view and shared sdf.environment producer, with a still view rendered once and identical pass work on both backends
binding: The positive leg boots a still 64 by 64 offscreen world with one demanded SDF view and indirect lighting explicitly Off. It waits for world.wait ready, reads world.counters gpu sixty completed ticks later, waits thirty more ticks and reads again. The world view keeps submission 1 in both reads; main advances from submission 64 to 94. The shared world$environment producer keeps submission 1. Counter presentation follows instance registration order, so world$environment appears after main even though the dependency graph executes its reductions before their consumers. The residency line sdf:world reports its latest completed upload, submission 2. Fillers initialize on the first upload alone, and their line therefore reads skipped in these observations; that initialization remains residency work. Bricks also reads skipped because this fixture bakes no brick. Upload executes. The residency environment row now counts the CPU procedural candidate projection decision, not GPU map and coefficient dispatches; it reads skipped in this latest unchanged upload. GPU environment production belongs to the separate sdf.environment package on world$environment. Its map and coefficients passes each dispatch once for the default fog's environment, and its screens pass dispatches once to initialize the shared screen-radiance records. With no acquired emitting images, that kernel writes zero cell means and whole-image means. Those initialized buffers and their submitted publication are real work, and the still producer lets them stand afterward. The view's twelve sdf.world passes appear in fragment order, mask through composite. The mesh, ambient and shadow passes skip; the empty-field tape exits without shape work; cull arguments marches nothing and writes no texel. Primary, surface and views dispatch indirectly over 256 texels, while sky and composite write 4096 pixels. Each executed pass carries its planned barriers, pass-block upload and kernel counters, and zero command buffers; recording belongs to the node's one command list. The detail rows subdivide pass work and add no upload allowance. Sky's gradient row carries 4096 evaluations and its lowest run carries 4096 written texels; upper runs carry zero. Composite reads the environment map for fog, evaluates no sky, and counts the one base-image tap at each output pixel. The exact empty-field view and root rows carry zero secondary-shadow, environment-candidate, indirect and primitive work. The first-frame upload correction remains sealed: mask uploads 1904 bytes, beam, tape, cull arguments, primary and surface 1908 each, views 1912, and sky and composite 1920 each, totaling 17196 bytes across the nine executed view passes. Finite light-map, indirect source/receiver and cache publication fields grew the world block, and independent sky extents and fitted infinity records grew the sky block. Initial region contents and bounded changed-word run coalescing account for the uploads, including gaps between paired runs. The deliberate block growth adds 1476 bytes to each of seven world passes and 1480 to sky and composite, 13292 bytes in all. Sky and composite each bind the eight fitted infinity-image slots, using sampled fillers when this default stack contains no view layer. Together with their existing port and screen-source bindings, this raises first-recording descriptor writes from 48 to 56 for sky and from 49 to 57 for composite. Views consumes three named current environment buffers: coefficients, map and screen reduction. Their host-to-compute acquisitions account for three additional buffer barriers. Views also publishes its existing visibility allocation through a preserving writable successor, even with indirect Off; composite must order its subsequent visibility read after that writer, accounting for its new one buffer barrier. Repeated read-only consumption of the environment buffers adds no further composite barrier. Views has four buffer barriers: one combined visibility read/write acquisition and three environment acquisitions. Compatible accesses to the same buffer storage and frame role within one pass form one incoming access, so the visibility predecessor read and preserving successor write share one barrier before the dispatch. The resulting read/write state still orders composite's later visibility read. Version dependencies and input/output ports remain distinct in the graph. Pipeline and shader-module creation belongs to gpu.pass-pipelines, not either node. Its exact totals are 21 pipelines and 23 modules: sixteen SDF compute kernels, the brick baker leased with the residency's brick pool, the device region-copy pipeline, the one place pipeline shared by main's four passes, and the mesh and impostor graphics pipelines with two modules each. The additional compute pipeline and single module are sdf-screen-emission, actually bound and dispatched by sdf.environment$screens to establish the initial reduction. Indirect classify, trace, shade and light-view kernels are demand-built and are not the cause in this Off fixture. Residency creates two filler images; the view creates ten images, its three output slots, mesh visibility and depth, lit image and four sky-run images. The environment node creates no image or node-owned pipeline/module. Device residency upload details and created buffers, pools and sets remain named without device-independent exact pins. Main's four place passes dispatch nothing and report their exact planned barriers with zero march and texel work. The discriminating leg reads world.counters gpu twice before the first tick, so no completed submission or upload row is available. It keeps its own absence assertions and turns the positive's submission extractions and executed-row assertions red. The remaining replacement rows and environment pass ordering follow the supplied backend observations; the corrected Views total is asserted with the combined-access planner fix.
